summary: Draft. Of the five selected clinics, I could read three websites: Studio B Dental, North York Smile Centre and Dr. Neil J. Gajjar Associates & Specialists. Two of the three publish implant prices before the enquiry, and all three ask visitors to send a request and wait to be contacted rather than book a confirmed time. In the public ad libraries, Studio B Dental had an All-on-X ad active when checked whose fee is worded differently from its website, North York Smile Centre's active Meta ads were for Invisalign while most of its observed posts were about full-arch implants, and Dr. Gajjar's active Meta ads promoted general dental care. Dundas East Dental's and Bond Street Dental's websites could not be read and the Instagram evidence is an incomplete sample, so this page is not a finished comparison.

findings.title: Two of the three readable clinics publish implant prices before the enquiry
findings.text: Studio B Dental and North York Smile Centre both give figures for a single implant and for full-arch treatment. North York Smile Centre sets out three full-arch levels per arch, each tied to a restoration material and shown with a monthly figure on approved credit. Studio B Dental gives a starting fee on its All-on-X page and a different full-set range on another implant page. Dr. Gajjar's implant page gives no figure and closes with a call to schedule a consultation. Studio B Dental's All-on-X ad in Meta Ad Library, active when checked, gives a per-arch figure and prices a final bridge separately, while its website gives a different starting fee and, in the text I saved, no separate fee for the final bridge. The two do not describe their inclusions in the same way, so the difference is unresolved.
findings.limitation: Published starting prices are the clinics' own statements with different inclusions, so they are not comparable with each other. I saw the ad and the page on the same day, which does not show which figure a patient is quoted, and two of the five clinics could not be read.
findings.takeaway: Cost is one of the first questions an implant patient has, and two of these clinics answer it before asking for contact details. Check that every price in your ads matches the page or message it leads to, with the same inclusions, and ask your team which cost questions the front desk hears every week.

findings.title: The consultation offer is described in very different detail
findings.text: Studio B Dental lists five appointment options with their length and fee, from a complimentary screening or second opinion to a paid two-visit exam, and its All-on-X page asks for a free screening and estimate. North York Smile Centre offers a free consultation and describes it as no-obligation. Dr. Gajjar's implant page asks visitors to call to schedule a consultation without saying what it includes or whether it has a fee.
findings.limitation: These are published offers. Whether staff describe them the same way on the phone, and how many people choose each option, cannot be seen from outside.
findings.takeaway: A patient deciding whether to enquire is also judging what the first visit will cost in time and money. Ask your team to write down what your implant consultation includes and costs, then check that your implant page and your phone script say the same thing.

findings.title: Every enquiry route I could read ends in a request, not a confirmed booking
findings.text: All three readable clinics ask the visitor to send details and wait to be contacted. Studio B Dental uses a virtual consult form that offers smile photo uploads; North York Smile Centre and Dr. Gajjar use appointment request forms that ask for a preferred date and time. North York Smile Centre explains the next steps on its home page, Studio B Dental says a team member will be in touch, and Dr. Gajjar's appointment request page does not say what happens next. None of the forms reviewed asks an implant question, such as how many teeth are missing or whether the person wears a denture.
findings.limitation: No form was submitted, so response times and follow-up are unknown. A stated promise is not a tested result.
findings.takeaway: Between the form and the first call, an implant enquiry can go cold, and a generic form tells your team little about the case before they call. Ask your team how long recent implant enquiries waited for a first reply, and whether your form tells people what happens next.

findings.title: Only one readable clinic had an implant ad active when checked
findings.text: Of the three clinics whose websites I could read, Studio B Dental was the only one with an implant ad active in Meta Ad Library when checked: an All-on-X offer, alongside a veneers offer. North York Smile Centre's active Meta ads were one Invisalign offer, while three of the five posts observed on its Instagram account were about full-arch implants, including a webinar invitation. Dr. Gajjar's Meta ads, started on 12 October, promote general dental care. Google Ads Transparency showed no ads for these three domains in the window; North York Smile Centre's implant ads there were last shown in November 2025.
findings.limitation: The ad libraries were searched by exact name and by domain on one day. An ad under another page name or pointing elsewhere would not appear, an active ad may not have run on every day of the window, and the Instagram posts are an incomplete sample. Nothing here shows budget or results.
findings.takeaway: What a clinic posts about and what it pays to promote are separate decisions. Ask your team which treatment each of your live ads promotes today, and whether that matches the treatment you most want enquiries for.

studiob.positioning: Full-arch replacement for people with failing teeth or dentures they dislike, under a same-day brand, Teeth-In-1-Day, with separate pages for single implants and metal-free zirconia implants.
studiob.observed: A starting fee on the All-on-X page with the two treatment phases spelled out, a price range on a second implant page, five consultation options with lengths and fees, a site-wide virtual consult form with optional smile photo uploads, an implant guide covering bone, pain and insurance, and the lead dentist named and described as teaching the procedure. Four posts were observed on its Instagram account in the window: one implant testimonial, one whose hashtags mention implant surgery and veneers, and two about cosmetic work and clinic life. Meta Ad Library showed two ads active when checked, an All-on-X offer and a veneers offer, both with library start dates before the window; Google Ads Transparency showed no ads for its domain.
studiob.supports: The website is built around one clinician and one full-arch offer, and it answers cost and consultation questions before asking for contact. My reading: the cost figures on different pages, and a different figure in the All-on-X ad, could leave a visitor unsure which applies. That is a reading of the published offers, not a measured effect.
studiob.unknown: Whether the account published other posts in the window beyond the four observed, play counts, whether the All-on-X ad ran on every day of the window, which fee a patient is quoted, the image galleries, and how the form is answered.
studiob.takeaway: When cost appears in more than one place, every figure needs to describe the same thing. Ask your team to list each implant price in your ads and on your site with what it includes, and check that they agree.

price_note.title: Two published full-arch fees: an unresolved difference

rows.label: Website, All-on-X page
rows.wording: "FEE: from $17,900", in the fee block that lists the first phase.
rows.scope: Phase 1 lists the removal of all upper or lower teeth with oral sedation, 4 to 8 titanium implants and a full set of teeth attached the same day as an immediate fixed temporary bridge, worn for up to 6 to 12 months. Phase 2 is a final bridge 4 to 12 months later; the saved page text gives no separate fee for it and does not say whether the starting fee covers it.

rows.label: Meta ad, Ad Library record
rows.wording: "$17,990 PER ARCH" for a package of extractions, four or more implants and a non-removable temporary bridge placed the same day.
rows.scope: A final bridge 4 to 6 months later is listed separately at $8,900. The ad also lists free consultations, a free panoramic X-ray and a free records appointment, and does not name the implant material. Active when checked; library start date 21 January 2026.

price_note.reading: I observed both on the same day. They differ in the starting figure, in the timing of the final bridge and in whether the final bridge is priced, and their inclusions may not match, so I do not add the amounts, call either figure wrong or compare it with other clinics. It is an unresolved difference between two published offers.

nysc.positioning: A family practice that gives full-arch implants their own page, opening with situations such as loose dentures and teeth that cannot be saved, alongside single-tooth implants.
nysc.observed: A single-implant range with what it includes, three All-on-X levels per arch tied to restoration materials and shown with monthly figures on approved credit, a named financing partner, a free, no-obligation consultation, a six-step treatment journey, the planning technology explained, an appointment request form with preferred date and time, and a three-step explanation of what happens after a request. Five posts were observed on its Instagram account in the window: three about full-arch implants (a patient testimonial, an All-on-X question reel and a webinar invitation), one about emergencies and one about Invisalign. Its Meta ads active when checked were one Invisalign offer; its implant ads in Google Ads Transparency, placed by OneCore Media Corp., were last shown in November 2025.
nysc.supports: Of the three websites I could read, this one sets out the fullest published picture of price and process: levels, materials, monthly figures and the steps from consultation to final teeth are all visible before the enquiry. Whether that changes who enquires is a hypothesis, not something public pages can show. My reading: the observed posts carry the implant message onto Instagram and offer a webinar as a lower-commitment next step than a consultation; whether that changes who enquires is not visible from outside.
nysc.unknown: Whether the account published other posts in the window beyond the five observed, play counts, how many people registered for or attended the webinar, what the active ads would have promoted on other days, and whether the reviews shown relate to implants.
nysc.takeaway: Tiered pricing turns one large number into a choice between levels. If you publish full-arch fees, test showing levels by material and measure which consultations go ahead and at what level, from your own records.

gajjar.positioning: A multi-specialty practice in Mississauga that covers single implants and All-on-4 or All-on-X on one page, framed around missing teeth and an evaluation of the right option.
gajjar.observed: Six questions and answers on candidacy, process, full-arch options, lifespan and bone loss, clinician profiles including a prosthodontist, no price or financing figure on the implant page, a call to schedule a consultation, and an appointment request form that requires a date, time, patient status and contact details. Its Instagram account refused my logged-out request, so no posts were read. Two Meta ads started on 12 October and promote general dental care in Mississauga. Google ads for its domain, placed by Optio Publishing Inc., were last shown on 31 May 2026 in the creatives I opened, and none was shown in the window.
gajjar.supports: The page leads with clinician credentials and plain answers rather than price or an offer. Because single-tooth and full-arch treatment share one page, its opening speaks to both situations at once.
gajjar.unknown: Instagram posts, whether implant ads ran in the window under another name or domain, the smile gallery's implant cases and how the form is answered.
gajjar.takeaway: Credentials answer who will treat the patient, but not what it will cost or what happens next. Ask your team which questions implant callers ask most, and whether your implant page answers them before the form.

I did not try to get past it, and nothing behind the panel was read. Its implant pages, clinician, location, Instagram account and prices are to be checked in an ordinary browser before anything is written here.
dundas.method_note: the home page showed a "VPN or Proxy Detected" panel on 16 October 2026, after an automated request was refused (HTTP 403); not reviewed. Its Meta and Google searches found no matching ads.

bond.reason: On 16 October 2026 dentalimplantsclinic.ca showed a Cloudflare security check, both to an automated request and in the headless browser, and I did not pass it. The website was not read, so its link to Bond Street Dental is not confirmed by the site itself. ad_note.text: Google Ads Transparency listed 26 ads from the verified advertiser Passion Dental Group Inc that pointed to dentalimplantsclinic.ca in the window. 12 of them name Bond Street Dental or show a Bond Street location or address, which supports, but does not confirm, a link between the domain and the clinic; the rest show only the domain. 3 are about implants, including a headline offering a dental implant at $1,599 with no conditions visible, and only one of those shows a Bond Street address. The group's ads are not credited to Bond Street Dental as a group.

patterns.title: Single-tooth and full-arch patients are addressed on separate pages at two clinics, on one page at the third
patterns.text: Studio B Dental and North York Smile Centre each give full-arch treatment its own page that opens with a full-arch situation, such as failing teeth or loose dentures, and keep single implants on another page. Dr. Gajjar covers both on one page under a missing-teeth heading. These are different patient situations with different costs and decisions, so a shared page has to speak to both at once.
patterns.takeaway: Someone searching for full-arch treatment and someone missing one tooth need different first answers. Ask your team where each implant ad, post and email link points, and whether full-arch traffic lands on a full-arch page.

patterns.title: Clinician-led proof at two clinics, process and technology at the third
patterns.text: Studio B Dental builds its implant pages around its lead dentist, whom it describes as performing and teaching the procedure. Dr. Gajjar's implant page carries the clinicians' credentials, including a prosthodontist. North York Smile Centre leads instead with its planning technology and a step-by-step treatment journey. All three describe their own experience in their own words; I have not verified those statements.
patterns.takeaway: Patients weighing a large treatment want to know both who will do it and what will happen. As a hypothesis to test, swap the first section of your implant page between a clinician introduction and a step-by-step journey for a few weeks each, and measure qualified implant enquiries per page visit from your own form and call records.

patterns.title: Outcome and experience claims appear without sources
patterns.text: Studio B Dental states a success rate and a five-year continuing care warranty; North York Smile Centre states that its team has placed thousands of implants and shows patient reviews that mostly describe other treatment. None of these statements links to a source or set of terms on the page reviewed.
patterns.takeaway: Claims carry more weight when a patient can see where they come from. Ask your team which claims on your implant pages you could document if a patient asked for the source or the terms.

patterns.title: Educational answers come before the contact prompt at all three
patterns.text: Each readable clinic answers common implant questions on or near its implant pages before asking for contact: Studio B Dental in an implant guide covering bone, pain and insurance, North York Smile Centre in an implant FAQ, and Dr. Gajjar in a page written entirely as questions and answers. Whether these pages appear in search results or AI answers was not checked.
patterns.takeaway: An answer is most useful when the next step sits right after it. Ask your team whether each of your implant answers ends with the matching next step, such as a cost page, the consultation details or the form.

patterns.title: Implant posts in the observed sample lead with patients and questions
patterns.text: In the observed sample, the implant posts are patient testimonials at Studio B Dental and North York Smile Centre and, at North York Smile Centre, an All-on-X question reel and a webinar invitation. Their calls to action differ: a direct message for a complimentary consultation, a call to book a consultation, and webinar registration. The videos were not watched, so this reads captions and visible covers only.
patterns.takeaway: An implant post helps only if an interested reader knows what to do next. Ask your team where each implant post sends someone, whether a consultation, a message or an event, and whether that next step is recorded so it can be counted.

tests.title: Show what full-arch treatment costs before the form (finding 1)
tests.evidence: Two of the three readable clinics publish implant prices before the enquiry; one sets out full-arch levels by material with monthly figures, one leads with a consultation instead, and one clinic's ad and website describe its full-arch fee differently.
tests.hypothesis: A clear cost block on the full-arch page, with starting prices and what each includes, may change who enquires: fewer enquiries from people who would stop at the price, and more who go on to a consultation.
tests.change: Add one cost block to your full-arch page: your starting prices, what each includes and your financing route.
tests.constant: Ads, budgets, targeting, the rest of the page, the form and how quickly your team replies.
tests.measure: Share of full-arch enquiries that reach a completed consultation, from your own records.
tests.guardrails: Total full-arch enquiries, and cost per completed consultation if you run ads. Prices must be accurate and match what the front desk quotes and what your ads say.
tests.compare: Compare a fixed period before and after the change, each given the same follow-up time so slow-moving enquiries can complete. This is a before-and-after comparison, not a controlled split test, so note anything else that changed, such as season or ad spend.
tests.insufficient: Too few full-arch enquiries in either period to tell a difference from normal variation, or a large change in ads or season during the test. Extend the test rather than draw a conclusion.

tests.title: Say what the implant consultation includes (finding 2)
tests.evidence: One readable clinic lists its consultation options with length and fee, one offers a free no-obligation consultation, and one asks visitors to call without saying what the consultation includes.
tests.hypothesis: Stating what the first visit includes, how long it takes and whether it costs anything may increase the share of enquiries that book and attend a consultation.
tests.change: Add a short consultation description beside the main call to action on your implant page.
tests.constant: The consultation itself, its price, the form, ads and reply times.
tests.measure: Share of implant enquiries that book and then attend a consultation.
tests.guardrails: No-show rate, and staff time spent explaining the consultation on the phone.
tests.compare: Compare equal periods before and after, counting only enquiries old enough to have had the same time to book and attend. If your website tool can split visitors between two versions at random, that is stronger than a before-and-after comparison.
tests.insufficient: Too few implant enquiries to separate the change from normal week-to-week variation, or a change to the consultation offer itself during the test.

tests.title: Ask one implant question on the enquiry form (finding 3)
tests.evidence: None of the forms reviewed asks an implant question; all three readable clinics rely on general contact and appointment fields, and one adds optional smile photos.
tests.hypothesis: One short multiple-choice question, such as one missing tooth, several, all teeth in one jaw, or a denture, may let your team prepare a better first call and raise the share of implant enquiries that reach a consultation.
tests.change: Add one optional multiple-choice question about the patient's situation to the implant enquiry form.
tests.constant: Every other form field, page content, ads and reply times. Keep the question optional so it does not block an enquiry.
tests.measure: Share of implant enquiries that reach a completed consultation, and the time from enquiry to first contact, from your own records.
tests.guardrails: Form completion rate and total enquiries. Do not ask for clinical photos or health details in the form without the right privacy handling.
tests.compare: Compare equal periods before and after the change, with equal follow-up time for each enquiry. Treat it as a before-and-after comparison, not a controlled split test.
tests.insufficient: Too few implant enquiries to compare, a fall in form completions that offsets any gain, or answers that are mostly left blank.
